items.title: Tensor Maxwell equations equal the four laboratory Maxwell equations
items.statement:
Let the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ with its inertial chart $x$, the electric and magnetic fields $E,B$ of [[def-em-fields]], the source fields $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]] with $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be those of the framework, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with the components fixed there, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let $j=(cho,J)$ carry the tensor-component identification adopted in [[def-em-sources]]. Assume the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]: $E,B$ are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega	imes I$ with the additional derivatives required by each displayed equation existing and continuous, and $ho,J$ are continuous. Write $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ and $\partial_i$ for the coordinate partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and $\operatorname{div},\operatorname{curl}$ for those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then: (a) [Equivalence] On $I	imes\Omega$ the four smooth-branch equations $$\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ hold if and only if the two systems $$(\mathrm{TM1})\quad \partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0\,j^
u\ (
u=0,1,2,3),\qquad (\mathrm{TM2})\quad \partial_\lambda F_{\mu
u}+\partial_\mu F_{
u\lambda}+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\mu}=0\ (\lambda,\mu,
u\in\{0,1,2,3\})$$ hold on $I	imes\Omega$. Every instance of $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with a repeated index vanishes identically because $F$ is alternating, so $(\mathrm{TM1})$ and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ carry exactly eight independent scalar equations: $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=0$ is $\operatorname{div}E=ho/\varepsilon_0$ (using $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$), $(\mathrm{TM1})$ with $
u=i$ is the $i$-th component of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, $(\mathrm{TM2})$ with $(\lambda,\mu,
u)=(1,2,3)$ is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and the three cyclic triples $(0,i,j)$ are the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$; conversely these eight scalar equations reproduce the two systems. (b) [Form invariance under a change of inertial description] Let $x'$ be another inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$, $\Lambda$ a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix (the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]), and let the primed components of the same objects be the tensor components of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii): $F'^{\,ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$, $F'_{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a(\Lambda^{-1})^d{}_bF_{cd}$, $j'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bj^b$. Then $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x$ if and only if $(\mathrm{TM1})$ holds in $x'$ with $j'$, and $(\mathrm{TM2})$ holds in $x$ if and only if it holds in $x'$; by (a) applied in both charts the four smooth-branch equations are likewise form-invariant, the primed fields satisfying the primed equations with the primed sources. (c) [Hypotheses actually used] Only first derivatives of $E,B$ occur; the equivalence uses exactly the component dictionary, the alternating character of $F$, the constants $\mu_0,c,\varepsilon_0$ and the identification $j=(cho,J)$, and the covariance clause uses the constant-coefficient component law and the invertibility of $\Lambda$. No potential, no second derivative, no boundary, decay or smoothness hypothesis beyond the stated class, and no converse from the wave equations to the Maxwell equations is used or asserted. (d) [Scope] Only the smooth branch is covered; the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and field or source points of singular support are excluded. The conventions $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ fix the signs of $(\mathrm{TM1})$, and the alternative sign convention, which reverses the form of the sourced equation, is not mixed with them. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates, uses no choice principle and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation, then the transformation law. (a) Substitute the displayed components: $\partial_\mu F^{\mu0}=\partial_iF^{i0}=-\operatorname{div}E/c$ versus $-\mu_0j^0=-\mu_0c\rho$ gives $\operatorname{div}E=\mu_0c^2\rho=\rho/\varepsilon_0$; $\partial_\mu F^{\mu i}=\partial_0F^{0i}+\partial_jF^{ji}=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i-(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$ versus $-\mu_0j^i$ gives the $i$-th Ampère component; $\partial_1F_{23}+\partial_2F_{31}+\partial_3F_{12}=\operatorname{div}B$; and the cyclic sums $\partial_0F_{ij}+\partial_iF_{j0}+\partial_jF_{0i}=c^{-1}\left(\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_tB_k+\partial_iE_j-\partial_jE_i\right)$ for the three cyclic pairs $(i,j)$ give the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$. Each display is an identity after substituting the components, so both implications follow; no derivative is commuted and no epsilon-identity beyond the coordinate definition of the components is used. (b) For $(\mathrm{TM1})$: $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=(\Lambda^{-1})^c{}_a\Lambda^a{}_e\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{ef}=\Lambda^b{}_f\partial_cF^{cf}$ by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iv) and orthogonality $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$, so $\partial_cF^{cf}=-\mu_0j^f$ is equivalent to $\partial'_aF'^{ab}=-\mu_0j'^b$. For $(\mathrm{TM2})$ the three derivative factors contribute the same trilinear factor $(\Lambda^{-1})^{\otimes3}$ to the cyclic sum, and $\Lambda^{-1}$ is invertible; hence zero is preserved in both directions. No physical equivalence of descriptions is proved: clause (b) is conditional on the adoption of [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]].
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth branch of the adopted vacuum Maxwell postulate on the laboratory region: the four SI Maxwell equations are equivalent to the two tensor equations for the components of the electromagnetic two-form and four-current fixed by [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and [[def-em-sources]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $x^0=ct$, $\mu_0c^2\varepsilon_0=1$, and form-invariance under proper orthochronous changes of inertial chart. Excluded: the weak branch, singular source support, magnetic charge, potentials, and any dynamics beyond the adopted equations; no empirical claim.

items.title: Covariance, boosts and the two field invariants
items.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart $x$ of the framework ([[def-em-lab-geometry]]), $k\ge1$, with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $\Lambda_\beta$ be the explicit boost of [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]] with $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_0=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_1=\gamma$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^0{}_1=\Lambda_\beta{}^1{}_0=-\gamma\beta$, $\Lambda_\beta{}^2{}_2=\Lambda_\beta{}^3{}_3=1$ and all other entries zero. Let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the corresponding inertial chart, and for every event $p$ in the overlap of the two chart restrictions define the primed field components by reading the components of the same $F$ in $x'$ through the dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], so that $F'_{0i}=-E'_i/c$, $F'_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B'_k$ at $p$. Then: (a) [Boosted fields] at every such $p$, with $\parallel$ and $\perp$ the components along and orthogonal to $e_1$ in the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart, $$E'_1=E_1,\quad B'_1=B_1,\qquad E'_\parallel=E_\parallel,\quad B'_\parallel=B_\parallel,\qquad E'_\perp=\gamma\,(E+v\times B)_\perp,\qquad B'_\perp=\gamma\,(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp,$$ equivalently, componentwise, $E'_2=\gamma(E_2-\beta cB_3)$, $E'_3=\gamma(E_3+\beta cB_2)$, $B'_2=\gamma(B_2+\beta E_3/c)$, $B'_3=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$. (a′) [Arbitrary boost direction] For a velocity vector $v\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|v|<c$, use the actual vector boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]], with $\gamma_v=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. If $v\ne0$, decompose the fields along $\widehat v=v/|v|$ and its orthogonal complement. Then $E'_\parallel=E_\parallel$, $B'_\parallel=B_\parallel$, $E'_\perp=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)_\perp$ and $B'_\perp=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)_\perp$. Equivalently, for every $v$, including $v=0$, $$E'=\gamma_v(E+v\times B)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot E)}{c^2},\qquad B'=\gamma_v(B-v\times E/c^2)-\frac{\gamma_v^2}{\gamma_v+1}\frac{v(v\cdot B)}{c^2}.$$ At $v=0$ these are the identity and no preferred parallel direction is assigned.  (b) [Invariants] at every such $p$, $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=E\cdot B;$$ equivalently the scalar fields $I_1:=\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $I_2:=F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=4\,E\cdot B/c$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) take the same values whether computed from the components in $x$ or in $x'$. (c) [General proper orthochronous changes] for any proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix $\Lambda$ with chart $x'=\Lambda x+b$, the primed components of $F$ are given by the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii), $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$; in particular, if $\Lambda=\widehat R$ is the extension of a spatial rotation $R$ of the frame ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), then $E'=RE$ and $B'=RB$, and by the unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii) every proper orthochronous change acts first by $(E,B)\mapsto(RE,RB)$ and then by the arbitrary-direction boost law (a′) with velocity $-c\beta$, where $\beta$ is the vector parameter of that factorization. The axis-only law (a) is not substituted for a general vector boost. (d) [Form invariance of the Maxwell branch] if $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in $x$ on the overlap, and $(\rho',J')$ are the components of the same four-current in $x'$, then $(E',B',\rho',J')$ satisfy the same four equations in $x'$, by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]. (e) [Scope] All clauses are pointwise on the overlap $U\cap U'$ of the two chart restrictions, are conditional on the adopted postulates, and concern the smooth classical flat branch; no accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, material medium, apparatus or empirical claim is involved; the transformation is exact algebra, and the primed component functions are $C^k$ wherever the overlap is open. The invariants clause uses only the proper orthochronous changes of description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; orientation-reversing changes are outside the framework's field conventions ([[def-em-fields]]).
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** component computation from the transformation law, then the scalar contractions. (a) Apply $F'^{ab}=\Lambda^a{}_c\Lambda^b{}_dF^{cd}$ ([[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii); $\Lambda_\beta$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map by [[lem-em-boost-preserves-metric]]) to the raised components: $F'^{01}=\Lambda^0{}_0\Lambda^1{}_1F^{01}+\Lambda^0{}_1\Lambda^1{}_0F^{10}=\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)F^{01}=F^{01}$, $F'^{02}=\gamma(E_2/c-\beta B_3)$, $F'^{03}=\gamma(E_3/c+\beta B_2)$, $F'^{12}=\gamma(B_3-\beta E_2/c)$, $F'^{13}=\gamma(-B_2-\beta E_3/c)$, $F'^{23}=F^{23}$. Reading $E'_i=cF'^{0i}$ and $B'_k$ from the appropriate cyclic entries through the dictionary gives the displayed components; the vector form evaluates $v\times B$ and $v\times E$ from [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (a′) For $v\ne0$ put $u=v/|v|$. Choose a coordinate vector $e_j$ not parallel to $u$, set $a=(e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u)/|e_j-(e_j\cdot u)u|$ and $b=u\times a$. Direct cross-product coordinates show $(u,a,b)$ is an oriented orthonormal basis. Let $R$ have these vectors as rows, so $Ru=e_1$, $R^{\mathsf T}R=I$ and $\det R=1$; only one finite choice is used. Substituting the matrix of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $B(v/c)=\widehat R^{-1}\Lambda_{|v|/c}\widehat R$. Apply the rotation component law proved in (c), then the axis computation (a), then rotate back. The determinant-one cofactor identity gives $R(p\times q)=(Rp)\times(Rq)$, yielding the parallel/perpendicular formulas. Use $\gamma_v-1=\gamma_v^2|v|^2/(c^2(\gamma_v+1))$ to combine the pieces into the displayed nonsingular vector formulas; at zero the separately defined boost is the identity.  (b) The two expressions are the two independent scalar contractions of the two-form; substituting the component law into $\tfrac12F_{ab}F^{ab}$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}$ with $\eta'=\eta$ shows invariance, equivalently clauses (c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], and [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] (b) identifies them with $|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ and $4E\cdot B/c$. (c) For the rotation case $\Lambda^0{}_0=1$, $\Lambda^0{}_j=\Lambda^i{}_0=0$, $\Lambda^i{}_j=R^i{}_j$ give $F'^{0i}=R^i{}_jF^{0j}$ and $F'^{ij}=R^i{}_kR^j{}_lF^{kl}$; reading the dictionary and using $\det R=1$ in the cofactor identity $\epsilon_{nij}R^i{}_kR^j{}_lR^n{}_m=\epsilon_{klm}$ ([[def-determinant-of-a-linear-operator]], [[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]) gives $E'=RE$, $B'=RB$. The general case is the actual unique factorization $\Lambda=B(-\beta)\widehat R$ of [[thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra]] (iii). Since components transform by multiplication with $\Lambda$, first apply $\widehat R$ and then $B(-\beta)$; the latter uses (a′) with vector velocity $-c\beta$, not the nonnegative axis parameter of (a). (d) Chain clauses (a)-(c) with [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]]: clause (a) of that theorem in both charts plus its clause (b) for the pair of descriptions. No potential, no second derivative of the fields, no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement on the smooth branch of the framework's Maxwell fields in one inertial chart: the exact passive-boost component formulas for $E,B$ along one spatial axis and in every vector direction (including the zero boost), invariance of $B^2-E^2/c^2$ and $E\cdot B$ under every proper orthochronous change of inertial description, the rotation and general-factorization laws, and form-invariance of the four Maxwell equations. Excluded: accelerating coordinates, curved spacetime, media, weak or singular fields, orientation-reversing changes, apparatus and any measurement or empirical claim.

items.title: Observer field split and exact classical wave Doppler reading
items.statement: Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^k$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of an inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] in SI units ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), $k\ge1$, and let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $n\in V$ be a future unit observer vector, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$ and positive rest metric ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (c)), and suppose its coordinate velocity in the laboratory frame is $w$, $|w|<c$, so that $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$ with $\gamma_w:=(1-|w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (d)-(e)). Then: (a) [Observer split and measured vectors] with $e_a:=F_{ab}n^b$, $b_a:=(*F)_{ab}n^b$ as in [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]], one has $e(n)=b(n)=0$, $e^\sharp,b^\sharp\in n^\perp$, the reconstruction $F=n^\flat\wedge e-*(n^\flat\wedge b)$ (so the six rest components $(e,b)$ determine $F$ at the event), and in the laboratory frame $$e_i=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}\bigl(E_i+(w\times B)_i\bigr),\qquad b_i=-\gamma_w\Bigl(B_i-\frac{(w\times E)_i}{c^2}\Bigr),\qquad e_0=-\frac{\gamma_w}{c^2}E\cdot w,\qquad b_0=\frac{\gamma_w}{c}B\cdot w.$$ Define the measured electric and magnetic vectors $E_n:=c\,e^\sharp$ and $B_n:=-b^\sharp$, the covectors first restricted to $n^\perp$ and raised with its positive rest metric (equivalently their spacetime metric-dual vectors, since both annihilate $n$); under the model assumption (A1) that an ideal field detector comoving with the observer at the reception event reads the components of $F$ in the observer's rest frame — equivalently that $E_n$ and $B_n$ are the electric and magnetic fields read there — the observed components are, in the observer's inertial rest frame, the arbitrary-direction boosted components of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′) for the vector parameter $\beta=w/c$: the components along $w$ equal $E_\parallel$ and $B_\parallel$, and the components perpendicular to $w$ equal $\gamma_w(E+w\times B)_\perp$ and $\gamma_w(B-w\times E/c^2)_\perp$. At $w=0$ the observer is the laboratory rest observer and reads $E,B$ themselves; there is no distinguished direction of motion. Orthogonality means $e(n)=b(n)=0$, not vanishing temporal covector components in an unrelated laboratory frame. (b) [Plane wave and exact frequency reading] let $K>0$, $\omega=cK$, a unit vector $s$, and complex amplitudes $e_{\mathrm a},b_{\mathrm a}\in\mathbb C^3$ be the data of a plane wave of [[def-em-plane-wave-definition]] whose amplitude equations hold as in [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]], so that the pair is a source-free smooth Maxwell field and $s$ is the propagation direction. Then the phase covector with components $k_a=(-\omega/c,(\omega/c)s_1,(\omega/c)s_2,(\omega/c)s_3)$ in the laboratory frame is a nonzero future null covector, and under the ideal-plane-wave reading rule of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (ii) the observer reads the exact angular frequency $$\omega_n:=-c\,k(n)=\gamma_w\Bigl(1-\frac{w\cdot s}{c}\Bigr)\omega>0,$$ with the direction transformation (aberration), longitudinal formulas and two transverse protocols of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] (i)-(v) apply with their nonzero-motion qualifications; at $w=0$ frequency and direction are unchanged. Successive inertial changes act on the same phase covector by [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii); each stage updates the direction as well as the frequency, and positive successive frequency ratios multiply. This composition statement is a direct covector/reading calculation, not a nonexistent composition clause of the Doppler supplier. (c) [Status and scope] the observer split, the nullity of $k$ and the frequency formula are conditional deductions from the stated items, while the identification of $(E_n,B_n)$ and of $\omega_n$ with apparatus readings is the explicitly adopted ideal-detector model assumption (A1) together with the ideal-plane-wave model [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] for the clock and light readings); no calibration, apparatus, statistical or empirical claim is made, no photon model and no identification of frequency with energy by a factor $\hbar$ is used, and the statement is pointwise at a reception event: the decomposition and the reconstruction of clause (a) hold pointwise for any future unit observer $n$, while the frequency and aberration readings of clause (b) are stated for inertial observers — an accelerating observer requires its own analysis, since differentiating the decomposition adds derivatives of $n$ — and media, dispersion, modulation, boundaries and finite line widths are outside the item.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** evaluate the observer decomposition of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] at the given $n$, then apply the exact SR Doppler theorem to the wave data. (a) Directly evaluate the adopted dictionary at $n=\gamma_w(1,w/c)$: $e_0=-\gamma_w E\cdot w/c^2$, $e_i=\gamma_w(E_i+(w\times B)_i)/c$. The dual dictionary is $(*F)_{0i}=B_i$, $(*F)_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}E_k/c$, so $b_0=\gamma_w B\cdot w/c$ and $b_i=-\gamma_w(B_i-(w\times E)_i/c^2)$. In particular $n^ae_a=n^ab_a=0$, using $w\cdot(w\times B)=w\cdot(w\times E)=0$; antisymmetry gives the same annihilation intrinsically. Raising with the spacetime metric maps these annihilating covectors into $n^\perp$, and its restriction agrees with the positive rest-space musical isomorphism. The reconstruction is exactly [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] (a). The vector boost [[def-lorentz-boost]] with parameter $w/c$ sends $n$ to $(1,0,0,0)$: its temporal component is $\gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2)=1$ and the spatial block cancels. Thus its primed oriented axes are the observer's canonical inertial rest axes. Apply the repaired arbitrary-direction law [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] (a′); in those axes $e'_0=b'_0=0$, $E'_i=c e'_i$ and $B'_i=-b'_i$, giving exactly the measured-vector components under assumption (A1). For $w=0$ the boost is the identity. No rest-space metric lowering can erase a nonzero laboratory component; the two component descriptions are distinct. (b) The amplitude equations give $|k|=\omega/c$ and $s=k/|k|$ with $|s|=1$ ([[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]] (b)); raising with $\eta$ gives $k^0=\omega/c>0$, $k^i=(\omega/c)s^i$ and $\eta(k^\sharp,k^\sharp)=-(\omega/c)^2+(\omega/c)^2|s|^2=0$, so $k$ is future null and nonzero. The data $(\omega,s)$ therefore satisfy the hypotheses of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]], whose clauses (i)-(v) give $\omega_n=\gamma_w(1-w\cdot s/c)\omega>0$, the aberrated direction and the longitudinal/transverse cases; the reading rule is clause (ii) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. For successive changes $x_1=\Lambda_1x_0+b_1$, $x_2=\Lambda_2x_1+b_2$, the covector laws give $k_2=(\Lambda_2^{-1})^{\mathsf T}(\Lambda_1^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0=((\Lambda_2\Lambda_1)^{-1})^{\mathsf T}k_0$. The affine phase constant transforms with the translations as in [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (ii). Apply the positive frequency reading at each stage, obtaining $\omega_2/\omega_0=(\omega_2/\omega_1)(\omega_1/\omega_0)$ with the correctly updated intermediate direction. (c) records the adopted interpretation premise (A1) and the scope; no choice principle is used and no empirical premise enters.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about the smooth framework fields at one event: the decomposition of the field into the rest components of a future unit observer, the reconstruction of $F$, the measured electric and magnetic vectors of an inertial observer with coordinate velocity $w$, and the exact angular-frequency reading and aberration of an ideal plane wave, with the ideal-detector and ideal-plane-wave model assumptions stated. Excluded: apparatus calibration, real detectors, accelerated observers, media and dispersion, modulation, finite line widths, intensity and polarization measurement, quantum photon models, and any statistical or empirical claim.

items.title: The four-force equation reproduces the coordinate Lorentz force and power
items.statement: Assume the framework's spacetime, field and worldline objects of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and clause (i) of the adopted Lorentz coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]: a constant charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-sources]] (a), an externally supplied rest mass $m>0$, a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline $x:J\to A$ with four-velocity $U$, and a prescribed field $F$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle; the adopted equation of motion is $$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),\qquad \eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u),$$ $U$ the four-velocity of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (b) with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $t\mapsto r(t)$ be the laboratory chart reading of the worldline, $v:=r'$ its coordinate velocity and $\gamma:=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, so that $U=\gamma(c,v)$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)). Then, wherever the worldline is $C^2$: (a) [Coordinate force and power] with the coordinate three-momentum $p:=m\gamma v$ of [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a), $$\frac{dp}{dt}=q\,(E+v\times B),\qquad \frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=q\,E\cdot v,$$ the derivatives taken with respect to the chart time $t$ and $E,B$ the components of $F$ in the laboratory frame. (b) [Norm preservation] $s\mapsto\eta(U(s),U(s))$ is constant on $J$ with value $-c^2$; in particular a solution with future timelike initial data remains future timelike, and $|v(t)|<c$ wherever the reading is differentiable ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]). (c) [Controlled low-speed expansion] for every $\delta\in(0,1)$, on any interval where $|v|/c\le\delta$, $$|\gamma-1|\le\frac{|v|^2/c^2}{2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma-1-\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\Bigl(\frac{|v|^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{2},$$ and consequently $$|p-mv|\le m|v|\,\frac{|v|^2}{2c^2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2}},\qquad \Bigl|\gamma mc^2-mc^2-\tfrac12m|v|^2\Bigr|\le\frac{3}{8}(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}\frac{m|v|^4}{c^2};$$ the constants depend only on $\delta$, so the bounds are uniform in $|v|/c\le\delta$. These are pointwise algebraic expansions; they assert no approximation of the trajectory over a time interval, which would require a separate stability argument. (d) [Scope] The charge is constant, $m>0$ is an externally supplied parameter and $F$ is a prescribed exterior field: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and any self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles and zero or variable mass; the nonrelativistic coordinate law is not adopted as exact, and (c) is a controlled kinematic expansion, not a trajectory approximation. The statement is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
items.strategy: **Proof technique:** contract the field with the four-velocity in the fixed component dictionary, then apply the mean value theorem to $(1-z)^{-1/2}$. (a) With $\Phi(u)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\alpha}F_{\alpha\beta}u^\beta$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]) and $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $U_\nu=\gamma(-c,v)$: $q\,\Phi(U)^i=q\gamma\bigl(cF^i{}_0+F^i{}_jv^j\bigr)=q\gamma(E_i+(v\times B)_i)$ since $F^i{}_0=\eta_{00}F^{i0}=E_i/c$ and $F^i{}_j=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$; and $q\,\Phi(U)^0=q\gamma E\cdot v/c$. Since $m\,dU^i/d\tau=q\Phi(U)^i$ and $d/dt=\gamma^{-1}d/d\tau$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]] (e)), $dp_i/dt=\gamma^{-1}\,q\gamma(E+v\times B)_i=q(E+v\times B)_i$ with $p=m\gamma v$ from [[pthm-sr-momentum-and-four-force]] (a); the temporal component gives $d(\gamma mc^2)/dt=qE\cdot v$ after multiplying by $c$. (b) $\eta(U,U)$ has derivative $2\eta(U,U')=2(q/m)\eta(U,\Phi(U))=0$ by the orthogonality clause of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] (which needs no derivative of the field); the initial value $-c^2$ is that of the four-velocity. For the stated solution-preservation conclusion, differentiability makes $U$ continuous and the norm identity gives $(U^0)^2=c^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2\ge c^2$. Thus $U^0$ cannot vanish; on a connected interval its sign cannot change by [[thm-intermediate-value]]. Positive initial $U^0$ therefore stays positive and the solution stays in the future timelike component. This conditional argument asserts no existence or continuation of solutions. (c) $z:=|v|^2/c^2$ and $f(z):=(1-z)^{-1/2}$; by [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]], $f'(z)=\tfrac12(1-z)^{-3/2}$ and $f''(z)=\tfrac34(1-z)^{-5/2}$ with $a^{-r}=(a^r)^{-1}$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]. At $z=0$ all stated differences and bounds are zero directly; henceforth assume $0<z\le\delta^2$. First-order bound by the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]): $|f(z)-1|=|f'(\xi)|z\le z\,/\,(2(1-\delta^2)^{3/2})$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, using monotonicity of the positive power ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], [[lem-of-inverse-positive]]). Second-order remainder by Cauchy's mean value theorem ([[thm-cauchy-mean-value]]) applied on $[0,z]$ to $q(s):=f(s)-1-\tfrac s2$ and $g(s):=s^2$: $q(z)/z^2=q'(\xi)/g'(\xi)=(f'(\xi)-\tfrac12)/(2\xi)$ for some $\xi\in(0,z)$, and the mean value theorem on $[0,\xi]$ applied to $f'$ gives $f'(\xi)-\tfrac12=f'(\xi)-f'(0)=\xi f''(\eta)$ for some $\eta\in(0,\xi)$, so $|f(z)-1-\tfrac z2|=\tfrac12|f''(\eta)|z^2\le\tfrac38(1-\delta^2)^{-5/2}z^2$. The two displays for $p$ and $\gamma mc^2$ are the multiplication of these bounds by $m|v|$ and $mc^2$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] for the product $p=m\gamma v$). (d) The scope clause records the postulates and exclusions; no choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement about one charged massive particle of constant charge and positive external rest mass moving on a future timelike $C^2$ worldline in a prescribed exterior electromagnetic field that is $C^1$ near the graph, under the adopted covariant coupling: the coordinate Lorentz force and power, preservation of the four-velocity norm, and uniform low-speed bounds with constants depending only on the speed interval. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction, self-force, magnetic monopoles, variable or zero mass, trajectory approximation over time without a stability argument, and any measurement or empirical claim.

items.title: The covariant field stress-energy tensor and its balance law
items.statement:
Assume the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I	imes\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]: $E,B$ jointly $C^1$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] with the additional derivatives required by each Maxwell equation existing and continuous, continuous sources $(ho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] with its fixed components, $j=(cho,J)$ the four-current, $u$ and $S$ the energy density and Poynting vector of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and $g$, $\sigma$, $\Pi=-\sigma$ the momentum density, Maxwell stress and momentum flux of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. Define the stress-energy tensor of the field by $$T^{\mu
u}:= rac{1}{\mu_0}\Bigl(F^{\mu\alpha}F^
u{}_\alpha- rac14\eta^{\mu
u}F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}\Bigr).$$ Then: (a) [Object] $T$ is a symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] with $\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}$ continuous on $U$, it is traceless, $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=0$, and under a proper orthochronous change of inertial chart with transition $x'=\Lambda x+b$ its components transform as $T'^{\mu
u}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^
u{}_ eta T^{\alpha eta}$ ([[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]], [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii)). (b) [Components] in the laboratory frame $$T^{00}=u= rac{\varepsilon_0|E|^2}{2}+ rac{|B|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=T^{i0}= rac{S_i}{c}=c\,g_i= rac{(E	imes B)_i}{\mu_0c},\qquad T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij},$$ where $\sigma_{ij}=\varepsilon_0 igl(E_iE_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|E|^2 igr)+\mu_0^{-1} igl(B_iB_j-	frac12\delta_{ij}|B|^2 igr)$; in particular the spatial block is minus the Maxwell stress of [[def-em-vacuum-stress-momentum]]. (c) [Balance] under the smooth branch, $$\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=-f^
u,\qquad f^
u:=F^{
u\lambda}j_\lambda,$$ where algebraically $f=(J\cdot E/c,ho E+J	imes B)$. Its interpretation as the electromagnetic four-force density delivered to matter uses the separately adopted continuum coupling [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii) for matter models and sources satisfying that postulate's hypotheses. The component identities are $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=-J\cdot E$ and $\partial_tg-\operatorname{div}\sigma=-(ho E+J	imes B)$ of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) [Matter coupling and finite-flux conservation] let $T_{\mathrm m}$ be a $C^1$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ field on $U$ satisfying $\partial_\mu T_{\mathrm m}{}^{\mu
u}=f^
u$ (an adopted matter model, not derived here); then $\partial_\mu(T+T_{\mathrm m})^{\mu
u}=0$, on every finite axis-parallel box with an open neighbourhood contained in $U$, the box and slice balance identities of [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] hold for the total tensor with zero divergence, retaining all side-flux terms. Constancy of a slice total requires that theorem's vanishing side-flux hypothesis; zero divergence alone does not supply it, and the angular current $M^{\lambda\mu
u}:=x^\mu T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda
u}-x^
u T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\lambda\mu}$ satisfies $\partial_\lambda M^{\lambda\mu
u}=0$ by symmetry. (e) [Scope] the divergence is a product identity of $C^1$ objects and is not asserted for the weak branch, at singular source support or for any product of distributions; symmetry, zero trace and the component display are algebraic; no matter tensor is derived from vacuum Maxwell, no radiation reaction or self-force is included, and no empirical claim is made.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct algebra from the components for (a)-(b); the product rule and the cyclic identity for (c); summation and the finite-box theorem for (d). (a) Symmetry: $\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu\alpha}F^{
u eta}=\eta_{\alpha eta}F^{\mu eta}F^{
u\alpha}$ by relabelling, and $\eta^{\mu
u}$ is symmetric; trace: $\eta_{\mu
u}T^{\mu
u}=\mu_0^{-1}(F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}-	frac14\cdot4\cdot F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta})=0$; the transformation law is contraction of two copies of the component law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] (iii) with $\eta$ invariant, and the regularity is the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] (every term is a polynomial in the $C^1$ components). (b) Substituting $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $F^{00}=0$: $T^{00}=\mu_0^{-1}(|E|^2/c^2+	frac14\cdot2(|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2))=\varepsilon_0|E|^2/2+|B|^2/(2\mu_0)$ using $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; $T^{0i}=\mu_0^{-1}F^{0j}F^i{}_j=(E	imes B)_i/(\mu_0c)$ with [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; $T^{ij}=-\sigma_{ij}$ by the component computation $\sum_k\epsilon_{ikm}\epsilon_{jkn}B_mB_n=\delta_{ij}|B|^2-B_iB_j$ and the negative temporal contraction of $F^{i0}F^{j}{}_0$. (c) Product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\mu_0\partial_\mu T^{\mu
u}=(\partial_\mu F^{\mu\alpha})F^
u{}_\alpha+F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^
u{}_\alpha-	frac12F^{\alpha eta}\partial^
u F_{\alpha eta}$; the first factor is $-\mu_0j^\alpha$ by [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]] ((TM1)), giving $-f^
u$; for the cancellation set $I=F^{\alpha eta}F_{\alpha eta}$ and fix a free index $\kappa$. Contract the cyclic identity $\partial_\mu F_{\kappa\alpha}+\partial_\kappa F_{\alpha\mu}+\partial_\alpha F_{\mu\kappa}=0$ with $F^{\mu\alpha}$. Its first and third terms both equal $C_\kappa:=F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F_{\kappa\alpha}$, the third by interchanging the dummy indices and using alternation twice; the middle term is $-F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\kappa F_{\mu\alpha}=-	frac12\partial_\kappa I$. Hence $C_\kappa=	frac14\partial_\kappa I$. Raise only this free index: $F^{\mu\alpha}\partial_\mu F^
u{}_\alpha=	frac14\partial^
u I=	frac12F^{\alpha eta}\partial^
u F_{\alpha eta}$, so the two product-rule terms cancel. The first term is $-\mu_0 j^\alpha F^
u{}_\alpha=-\mu_0 F^{
u\lambda}j_\lambda$, giving precisely $-f^
u$ after dividing by $\mu_0$. All repeated indices here are dummy indices and the free index is never reused in $I$. The component identities are (b) read in $(c)$; they coincide with the independently proved local identities of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] (a) and [[pthm-em-momentum-balance]] (a). (d) Add the matter equation; the finite box and slice balance identities, with side flux retained, are [[thm-sr-stress-balance-and-finite-flux]] applied to the $C^1$ symmetric total tensor with vanishing divergence; the angular identity uses $\partial_\lambda x^\mu=\delta^\mu_\lambda$ and the symmetry $T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{\mu
u}=T_{\mathrm{total}}{}^{
u\mu}$. The algebra gives $f^0=J\cdot E/c$ and $f^i=ho E_i+(J	imes B)_i$; identifying those source terms with matter work and force uses [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]] (ii) only in that interpretation. (e) records the regularity scope. No choice principle and no empirical premise are used.
items.physical_scope: Conditional statement on the smooth branch of the framework's Maxwell fields: the symmetric traceless stress-energy tensor quadratic in the field, its component identification with the energy density, Poynting flux, momentum density and Maxwell stress, the local balance $\partial_\mu T^{\mu\nu}=-f^\nu$ with the Lorentz four-force density, and conditional total conservation with an adopted $C^1$ symmetric matter tensor together with finite-box flux identities. Excluded: the weak branch, singular support, products of distributions, any derivation of a matter tensor from vacuum Maxwell, radiation reaction, self-force and any empirical claim.

items.title: Boosted uniform electric field and the mixed magnetic field
items.statement: Let $E_0>0$ carry the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ and consider the constant fields of [[def-em-fields]] $$E:\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3,\quad E\equiv E_0e_2,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ which form a source-free smooth solution of the vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] (all first derivatives vanish and $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}B=0$). Let $0\le\beta<1$, $\gamma:=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$ and $v:=\beta c\,e_1$, and let $x'=\Lambda_\beta x+b$ be the boosted inertial chart of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]]. Then the components of the same field in $x'$ are $$E'=\gamma E_0\,e_2,\qquad B'=-\frac{\gamma\beta E_0}{c}\,e_3=-\frac{\gamma |v|E_0}{c^2}\,e_3,$$ so the moving observer reads an electric field of magnitude $\gamma E_0$ along $e_2$ and, for $\beta>0$, a nonzero magnetic field along $-e_3$: a purely electric uniform field acquires a magnetic component in the boosted description. The two invariants check directly: with the spatial Euclidean structure of the chart ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) $$|B'|^2-\frac{|E'|^2}{c^2}=\gamma^2\Bigl(\frac{\beta^2E_0^2}{c^2}-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}\Bigr)=-\frac{E_0^2}{c^2}=|B|^2-\frac{|E|^2}{c^2},\qquad E'\cdot B'=0=E\cdot B,$$ using $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ ([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). At $\beta=0$ the formulas reduce to $E'=E$, $B'=0$. The computation is exact for the constant field; the example reports no measurement, identifies no source producing the field, and asserts nothing about finite-energy or bounded configurations.
items.strategy: **Verification:** substitute the data into clause (a) of [[pthm-em-lorentz-field-transform]] with $\beta$ as given. Here $E_\parallel=0$, $B_\parallel=0$ since $E\perp e_1$ and $B=0$, and $v\times B=0$, while $v\times E=(\beta c e_1)\times(E_0e_2)=\beta cE_0e_3$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the boost formulas give $E'=\gamma E_0e_2$ and $B'=-\gamma |v|E_0e_3/c^2=-\gamma\beta E_0e_3/c$. The invariant values are computed with [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the identity $\gamma^2(1-\beta^2)=1$ from [[lem-rational-power-laws]]; the constant field is a solution of the source-free smooth branch because every displayed first derivative vanishes. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: An exact algebraic example for one uniform static electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_2$, $B\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) and one passive boost along $e_1$ with $0\le\beta<1$: the boosted components, the resulting mixed magnetic field and the two field invariants. Excluded: real sources of the uniform field, boundary or finite-support configurations, measurements and any empirical claim.

items.title: Exact trajectory in a uniform electric field and the failure of the unscoped Newtonian extrapolation
items.statement:
Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter, $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass and $E_0>0$ a field strength in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and consider the prescribed exterior field of [[def-em-fields]] $$E\equiv E_0e_1,\qquad B\equiv0,$$ a source-free constant solution of the smooth vacuum Maxwell branch. Put $h:=qE_0/(mc)$, carrying the unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$, and for $r_0\in\mathbb R^3$ define the chart reading $t\mapsto(ct,r(t))$ by $$r(t):=r_0+ rac{c}{h} igl(\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}-1 igr)e_1\quad(h
e0),\qquad r(t):=r_0\quad(h=0),$$ $$v(t):=r'(t)= rac{c\,ht}{\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}}\,e_1\ (h
e0),\qquad \gamma(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2},\qquad p(t):=m\gamma(t)v(t).$$ Then: (i) [Exact solution] for $h
e0$ the curve is a future timelike $C^\infty$ curve with coordinate velocity $v(t)$, $|v(t)|<c$ for every finite $t$ and $|v(t)|	o c$ as $t	o\pm\infty$, and $p(t)=qE_0t\,e_1$, so that $$ rac{dp}{dt}=qE_0e_1=q(E+v	imes B),\qquad  rac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$$ hold identically, as required by [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (a); at $h=0$ (equivalently $q=0$) the curve is the constant $r\equiv r_0$ with $v\equiv0$, $p\equiv0$ and the same equations hold trivially. (ii) [Energy] $\gamma(t)mc^2=mc^2\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ and $ rac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$: the field delivers power $qE\cdot v$ to the particle. (iii) [Unscoped Newtonian extrapolation] For $h
e0$, the Newtonian constant-acceleration prediction $v_N(t):=(qE_0/m)t\,e_1$ satisfies $v(t)=v_N(t)/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$, so the two agree only to first order in $|ht|$ and $|v_N(t)|=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}\,|v(t)|$ exceeds $c$ for $|t|>1/|h|$, whereas the exact solution of the adopted coupling remains subluminal at every finite time; for this explicit solution the approximation is quantified directly. Put $r_N(t)=r_0+	frac12hc t^2e_1$. For $h
e0$, $$|v-v_N|\le rac c2|ht|^3,\qquad |r-r_N|\le rac{c}{8|h|}|ht|^4.$$ Thus on $|ht|\le\delta$ the velocity error is at most $c\delta^3/2$ and the displacement error at most $c\delta^4/(8|h|)$; these are special-model comparisons, not a general trajectory-stability consequence of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] (c). When $h=0$ both trajectories and velocities coincide, and the Newtonian superluminal-time condition containing $1/|h|$ is not used. (iv) [Scope] the field is prescribed and external, the particle's own field and any radiation reaction or self-force are excluded, and no measurement or empirical claim is made; the solution is exact for the stated coupling with $E_0>0$ and arbitrary constant $q$.
items.strategy: **Verification:** direct differentiation and substitution. For $h\ne0$ set $g(t):=\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$; by [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] and [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]] the map $t\mapsto(1+h^2t^2)^{1/2}$ is differentiable with $g'(t)=h^2t/g(t)$ ([[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]), hence $r'(t)=(c/h)g'(t)e_1=chte_1/g(t)=v(t)$ and $|v(t)|/c=|ht|/g(t)<1$ because $h^2t^2<1+h^2t^2$ ([[lem-of-square-monotone]]), with $|v(t)|\to c$ as $|t|\to\infty$. Then $p(t)=m\gamma(t)v(t)=mc\,ht\,e_1=qE_0t\,e_1$, so $dp/dt=qE_0e_1$, and $q(E+v\times B)=qE_0e_1$ since $B=0$ and $v\times0=0$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); the power identity is $\frac{d}{dt}(\gamma mc^2)=mc^2h^2t/g(t)=qE_0\,v_1(t)$. The curve is future timelike: its tangent $(c,v(t))$ has $\eta$-square $-c^2+|v(t)|^2<0$ with positive time component, in the sense of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] (a) and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the vector-valued derivative is [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. Part (iii) is the displayed identity $v=v_N/\sqrt{1+h^2t^2}$ with $v_N=(qE_0/m)te_1=hct\,e_1$, whose norm exceeds $c$ exactly when $|ht|>1$. For the direct error bounds let $s=ht$ and $g=\sqrt{1+s^2}\ge1$. Rationalization gives $g-1=s^2/(g+1)\le s^2/2$ and $1-g^{-1}=(g-1)/g\le s^2/2$. Since $v=v_N/g$ and $|v_N|=c|s|$, the velocity bound follows. Also $1+s^2/2-g=(g-1)^2/2\le s^4/8$, so multiplying its absolute value by $c/|h|$ gives the displacement bound. This directly proves the special-model approximation on the declared interval without importing a general stability claim. For $h=0$, $q=0$, $r=r_N=r_0$ and $v=v_N=0$, and every force/power identity is zero; no formula divides by $h$ in that branch. No measurement, empirical premise or choice principle is used.
items.physical_scope: An exact conditional solution example for one prescribed uniform external electric field ($E\equiv E_0e_1$, $B\equiv0$, $E_0>0$ in $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$) acting on a particle of constant charge $q$ and external rest mass $m>0$ under the framework's adopted covariant coupling: the trajectory, its subluminality at all finite times, the work-energy identity, and the comparison with the unscoped Newtonian constant-acceleration extrapolation. Excluded: the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force, the production of the field, measurement, and any empirical claim.
